title: The trailing equal sign of Base64 reveals the last set of valid bytes
summary: The presence of == at the end of the four-character group means that the last group contains only one original byte, and the occurrence of = means that it contains two.
detail: Normalized encoding requires that the last valid character does not carry the low-order zeros of the original text; therefore, the same after loose decoding does not mean that the original text is exactly the same.
boundary: In the unpadded format, the number of characters modulo 4 is 1, which cannot form legal and complete Base64 data.
relevance: Distinguish between missing outer padding and truly missing data when judging truncation or representation differences.
